to: Equus (E. asinus, E. quagga, E. grevyi, E. ferus)
reason: Same genus, same dichromatic ungulate plan; rule 2 cannot carry because the order Perissodactyla has only the horse measured.
source: squirrel-deer-rabbit#90 and #91 (Carroll 2001)

from: Bos taurus; Capra hircus; Ovis aries; Odocoileus virginianus; Dama dama
to: Camelidae, Giraffidae, Antilocapridae (Artiodactyla)
reason: Rule 2 holds only if the order Artiodactyla is read as measured in Bovidae and Cervidae (two families, both two classes, none disagreeing; pig also two); written here so the audit can accept it for camelids, giraffe and pronghorn, which have no pigment measurement of their own (giraffe has a gene prediction, #171).
source: squirrel-deer-rabbit#95, #96, #117, #118, #119; mammal-groups#125, #126

from: Odocoileus virginianus; Equus caballus; Rangifer tarandus
to: Bovidae, Camelidae, Giraffidae, Antilocapridae, Equus
reason: All three measured animals have a horizontal pupil and so do the ungulates in the survey the round-1 logs cite; sheep, goat, cattle and alpaca pupils are not logged. Pending: the species table of Banks 2015 (on the wanted list) before this is accepted.
source: squirrel-deer-rabbit#113, #116, #152; Banks 2015 supplementary table (not opened)

from: Felis catus; Acinonyx jubatus; Lynx rufus; Panthera pardus
to: Felidae
reason: S cones were labelled with an antibody in the cheetah, bobcat and leopard as well as the domestic cat, so a short-wavelength cone plus a long-wavelength cone is the family pattern; lion, tiger and cougar have no pigment measurement.
source: cat-dog#73, #138 (Guenther 1993; Ahnelt 2000)

to: Panthera (all species), Acinonyx jubatus
reason: Round pupil measured in tiger and in Pallas's cat and described as round for lion and large cats; the carry covers the genus Panthera by rule 3 and is extended to the cheetah on the strength of Banks 2015 (not opened), so keep it a proposal.

to: Canis latrans
reason: Congeneric canids with a round pupil and a pronounced visual streak in dog and wolf; coyote is not measured. Rule 3 covers the genus, listed here only because the dog view is lent to coyotes by family.

from: Canis lupus familiaris; Vulpes vulpes; Vulpes lagopus; Urocyon littoralis
to: Canis latrans; Canis lupus; Urocyon cinereoargenteus
reason: Three genera of Canidae measured at 429 to 435 nm and 555 nm (Jacobs 1993, Neitz 1989); one family only, so rule 2 does not apply; written as an exception for the species with no pigment measurement.

to: Lepus; Sylvilagus floridanus; Sylvilagus palustris
reason: Rabbit has two cone classes, a visual streak and a field of nearly 360 degrees; a broad streak is also measured in cottontails; hares have only a cone-presence finding. One family, so rule 2 cannot carry it.
source: squirrel-deer-rabbit#40, #73 to #81, #88

to: Sciurus (S. aureogaster, S. vulgaris and others)
reason: Rule 3 does not list photopigments but they follow the genus; both measured Sciurus are dichromats at about 444 to 450 and 540 to 543 nm.
source: squirrel-deer-rabbit#47, #48, #128, #129

from: Sturnus vulgaris, Turdus merula, Cyanistes caeruleus, Serinus canaria, Taeniopygia guttata
to: Passerida (cardinals, mockingbirds, wood-warblers, blackbirds, sparrows, finches)
reason: Five measured Passerida species in four families have an ultraviolet-type short-wave pigment and the sequenced Passerida are uniformly ultraviolet type, while the order Passeriformes as a whole contains violet-type crows and suboscines, so rule 2 at order level is blocked and a clade-level exception is needed.
source: birds-met evidence: Hart 2001 (Table 1); Odeen, Hastad and Alstrom 2011 (Passerida/Petroicidae homogeneous)

to: Anseriformes (whistling-ducks, teal, Muscovy duck, mergansers, geese, swans)
reason: Muscovy duck, brant and goosander all carry the violet-type short-wave opsin of the mallard (sequence, not measured pigment), and no Anseriformes member is known to differ; only one measured family exists, so rule 2 needs this exception.
source: birds-met evidence: Odeen and Hastad 2013 Table 1; Hart 2001 Table 1

to: Columbidae (mourning dove, Eurasian collared-dove, common ground dove)
reason: A fruit dove sequenced in Odeen and Hastad 2013 has the same violet-type opsin as the pigeon; one measured family only, so rule 2 does not reach the doves.
source: birds-met evidence: Odeen and Hastad 2013 Table 1 (Ptilinopus magnificus); Hart 2001 Table 1 (Columba livia)

from: Buteo jamaicensis, Parabuteo unicinctus, Buteo buteo, Milvus milvus, Accipiter nisus, Ictinia mississippiensis, Aviceda subcristata
to: Accipitriformes (red-shouldered hawk, osprey, bald eagle, snail kite, swallow-tailed kite)
reason: Violet-type short-wave cones are shown in the physiology of three raptors and the sequences of two more kites and hawks across Accipitridae; Pandionidae (osprey) has no entry, so the osprey needs this exception.
source: birds-met evidence: Lind et al. 2013 (round 1); Odeen and Hastad 2013 Table 1

to: Coragyps atratus
reason: Turkey vulture and black vulture share a family (Cathartidae) with identical retinal topography and peak resolving power in Lisney et al. 2013, so a violet-type opsin read from the turkey vulture is proposed for the black vulture.
source: birds-met evidence: Odeen and Hastad 2013 Table 1; round 1 record Lisney 2013

from: Ardea cinerea, Ardea herodias (field and bobbing)
to: Ardeidae (great egret, snowy egret, little blue heron, green heron, cattle egret)
reason: Heron head-bobbing depends on stride length, and the three heron fields measured (night heron, cattle egret, little egret) agree on a wide view below the bill, which rule 3 would restrict to the genus.
source: round 1 records: Necker 2007; Martin and Katzir 2008; Katzir and Martin 1998

to: Rostrhamus sociabilis, Elanoides forficatus, Ictinia mississippiensis
reason: NOT proposed as a carry: a measured black kite has one fovea where buteos have two, so the hawk view's row on two sharp spots is blocked for kites (rule 5) until a snail kite or swallow-tailed kite is measured.
source: round 1 record: Potier et al. 2016 (abstract)

to: Agkistrodon piscivorus; Sistrurus miliarius; Crotalus adamanteus
reason: All are pit vipers (Crotalinae) and the loreal pit is shared by the whole subfamily, which R1 lines from Crotalinae, Gloydius and Agkistrodon contortrix all show.
source: docs/views/evidence/herps.jsonl: Hartline 1978, Chen 2012, Moiseenkova 2003, Goris 2011

to: Dryophytes squirellus; Dryophytes gratiosus; Osteopilus septentrionalis; Anaxyrus terrestris; Acris gryllus
reason: Rule 2 reading: opsin gene repertoire (RH1, LWS, SWS1, SWS2; no RH2) was found in every one of the 33 anurans sampled, in several families, with no exception.
source: Schott RK et al. 2022, Ecology and Evolution, doi 10.1002/ece3.8595

from: Heliconius erato; Argynnis paphia; Speyeria aglaja
to: Dione vanillae; Heliconius charithonia; Euptoieta claudia
reason: Three genera of Heliconiinae each carry a red-opponent cell in red-shining ommatidia and no tested heliconiine lacks one, so the Gulf Fritillary and Zebra Longwing are likely to have a red channel; the row names the relatives and is graded g.
source: Belušič et al. 2021, Proc R Soc B, doi 10.1098/rspb.2021.1560, Table 1; Zaccardi et al. 2006, doi 10.1242/jeb.02207

to: Vanessa cardui; Vanessa virginiensis
reason: Red Admiral lacks the red-opponent cell and the filter pigments, and fails to tell red hues apart; congeners in the same genus share the eye plan (Painted Lady lambda max values are already logged in round 1), so a three-class eye without a red channel is carried within the genus.
source: Belušič et al. 2021 Table 1; Zaccardi et al. 2006 abstract

to: Danaus gilippus; Danaus eresimus
reason: Rule 2 cannot carry colour classes across Lepidoptera because Nymphalidae, Pieridae and Papilionidae disagree; within one genus the same opsins are expected, so the Queen takes the Monarch's three classes, orange filter pigment and red-opponent cell as a g row naming the Monarch.
source: van der Kooi et al. 2021 Table 1 (round 1); Belušič et al. 2021 Table 1

from: Hesperiidae (Horridge et al. 1972; Ocybadistes walkeri in Land 1997)
to: Hesperiidae (all skippers)
reason: Skippers have optical superposition eyes where other butterflies have apposition eyes; the one family measured is uniform in the studies logged, and skippers are 12.8 percent of butterfly records, so the butterfly view is wrong for them without this carry.
source: Horridge, Giddings & Stange 1972, doi 10.1098/rspb.1972.0088 (round 1 insect log); Land 1997 Table 1

from: Bombus impatiens; Bombus terrestris; Bombus lapidarius; Bombus hortorum
to: Bombus pensylvanicus; Bombus bimaculatus; Bombus griseocollis; Bombus fraternus
reason: Eleven Bombus species listed by van der Kooi et al. 2021 Table 1 fall in the same UV 329-355, blue 424-450, green 524-542 nm ranges; a range with the measured species named is carried to the genus.
source: van der Kooi et al. 2021 Table 1 (round 1 bee log)

from: Sympetrum striolatum; Libellula needhami; Anax junius; Hemicordulia tau
to: Pachydiplax longipennis; Erythemis simplicicollis; Perithemis tenera
reason: Rule 3 stops at the genus, but every libellulid measured (perching hunters) has a dorsal or frontodorsal acute zone and the three Florida skimmers hunt from perches in the same way; Switzer and Eason 2000 show the Amberwing detects intruders best straight ahead.
source: Land 1997 Table 1; Sherk 1978; Switzer & Eason 2000 abstract

from: Apis mellifera; Bombus (11 species); Osmia rufa; Vespula germanica; Polistes dominula; Vespa crabro; Anthophora acervorum; Andrena florea
to: Apidae; Megachilidae; Vespidae; Andrena (Halictidae are not covered: only Lasioglossum blue and green peaks are measured)
reason: Rule 2 is blocked for the whole order by two measured disagreements (Callonychium petuniae has a fourth class at 593 nm; the fire ant Solenopsis saevissima has a red class at 620 nm), so the three-class plan is carried family by family: UV, blue and green classes are measured in Apidae, Megachilidae, Andrenidae (Andrena) and Vespidae with no disagreement inside those families.
source: van der Kooi et al. 2021 Table 1 (closed, owner's Drive); logged in docs/views/evidence/insects-met.jsonl
